<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - Glance is a Go‑based, server‑rendered dashboard application (“single‑binary” web app) that reads a YAML configuration, fetches data from multiple external sources via modular “widget” plugins, renders HTML templates with embedded static assets (JS/CSS), and serves the result over HTTP or via Docker.  

2. Main Components  
   a. Entry Point / CLI (main.go & internal/glance/cli.go)  
   b. Configuration Loader (internal/glance/config.go & config‑fields.go)  
   c. HTTP Server & Router (internal/glance/glance.go + third‑party router if any)  
   d. Widget Engine (all widget‑*.go under internal/glance/)  
   e. Data Fetch & Cache (in‑memory caching inside each widget module)  
   f. Template Renderer (Go html/template files in internal/glance/templates + templates.go)  
   g. Static Asset Server (embedded CSS/JS/fonts/icons via internal/glance/static & embed.go)  
   h. System Info Provider (pkg/sysinfo)  
   i. External Services & APIs (RSS/Atom feeds, subreddits, weather API, Docker daemon, etc.)  

3. Relationships & Data Flow  
   - User Browser → HTTP Server (GET /)  
   - HTTP Server reads/validates YAML config → builds page model  
   - For each widget: Widget Engine checks cache → (if stale) → fetch data from External Service → parse/store in cache  
   - Template Renderer merges page model + widget data → produces HTML  
   - HTTP Server responds with HTML + inlined links to static assets  
   - Browser requests CSS/JS assets → Static Asset Server serves embedded files  

4. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Plugin‑style widget modules: each widget implements a common interface (init, fetch, render)  
   - MVC‑like separation:  
     • Model = configuration + fetched data  
     • View = Go‑templates + static assets  
     • Controller = HTTP handler routing + orchestrating widgets  
   - Embed pattern (Go 1.16+ go:embed) for assets → single binary  
   - Caching at widget level to minimize external calls  

5. Key Technologies & Libraries  
   - Go (modules)  
   - Go html/template  
   - go:embed for static assets  
   - YAML parsing (e.g., gopkg.in/yaml.v3)  
   - Docker (Dockerfile) / Docker Compose / goreleaser for packaging  
   - pkg/sysinfo for local system metrics  

6. Diagramming Guidelines Tailored to Glance  
   - Use layered view:  
     Layer 1 (Client): Browser  
     Layer 2 (Service): CLI → HTTP Server  
     Layer 3 (Core): Config Loader, Widget Engine, Cache, Template Renderer, SysInfo Provider  
     Layer 4 (External): APIs, Docker Daemon, RSS Feeds, Subreddits, Weather Services  
     Layer 5 (Assets): Embedded CSS/JS/Fonts/Icons  
   - Draw directional arrows:  
     • Browser → HTTP Server → Template Renderer → Browser  
     • Widget Engine ↔ External Services  
     • Widget Engine ← Cache → External Services  
     • HTTP Server → Static Asset Server → Browser  
   - Color‑code boxes:  
     • Blue = Core Go Services (HTTP Server, Widget Engine)  
     • Green = External Data Sources  
     • Yellow = Configuration & Cache  
     • Grey = Embedded Static Assets  

7. What to Include in the Diagram  
   - Clear labels for each component (e.g., “Widget Engine”, “Cache”, “Go‑Templates”)  
   - Arrows showing request/response and data‑flow direction  
   - Legend/key for color coding and shapes (rectangles for services, cylinders for cache, clouds for external APIs)  
   - Notation of the Go embed mechanism bundling “internal/glance/static” and “templates” into the binary  
   - Highlight the modular widget structure (group all widget‑*.go under one “Widget Modules” box with internal arrows showing plugin calls)  

8. Emphasis  
   - Capture every piece: CLI entry, config parsing, caching, widget fetch/render, templating, static‑assets serving, external integrations  
   - Do not over‑aggregate – show each major subsystem as its own shape  
   - Use consistent naming (match directory names: “internal/glance/config.go” = “Config Loader”)  

By following these guidelines, you’ll produce a comprehensive, accurate system‑design diagram that reflects Glance’s single‑binary Go architecture, its plugin‑style widget engine, templating system, caching layer, and integrations with external data sources.  
</explanation>
